newsitem.title: UK: C&W scorns cable delay report as "rubbish".
newsitem.headline: C&W scorns cable delay report as "rubbish".

text.p: Cable and Wireless, Britain's second biggest telecommunications company, on Monday denied as "rubbish" a newpaper report that its planned cable merger had been delayed because of growing disagreements between partners.
"The article is absolute rubbish," a company spokesman told Reuters. "We are on target for Spring 1997...and we shall announce the chief executive (of the new company) very soon."
The Independent said the proposed five billion stg merger between four cable firms -- C&W's Mercury subsidiary, NYNEX CableComms, Bell Cablemedia and Videotron -- had hit a series of obstacles.

The newspaper cited a clash of cultures, complexities of the merger and a lack of leadership at the new cable company, called Cable & Wireless Communications, as reasons why the merger was unlikely to be completed before the summer.

Cable and Wireless, which announced the planned merger last October, has consistently declined to comment on preferred candidates for the post of chief executive of the new company. Cable & Wireless Communications will be Britain's biggest cable group.
